body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 70f053d89212b5ecd0f43f9ff724d79bf0bb7eeb -->
**Independent review, #161 (static read of `origin/issue/110-pause-home` against #147; not built)**

Verdict: **2 BLOCKING**, plus notes.

The stop and home words look right. M1/M0 and the home moves come after M9/M5. They also come after `restorePlane()` and the G80 that closes any cycle. Z homes before XY: `G91 G28 Z0` / `G28 X0 Y0` / `G90` on Fanuc/Haas/Mazak, `G0 G53 Z0` then XY on 840D, and U before W on the lathe. The next section states its own S/M3 and coolant again, so a restart after M0 is clean. Skip is a pure post-time mask and undoes. Heidenhain refuses Go home.

### BLOCKING 1: suppressing an op ahead of a rest op posts rapids and full-engagement cuts into stock nothing judged
- `posting::program_ops` drops suppressed ops. But `rest::ahead_of` still walks `setup::operation_order`, which has no suppressed filter. So a later op's in-process stock still counts the suppressed op's cut. That covers its rest regions and the stock the generation-time vertical/linking rapid verdict judges against (rest.rs:321).
- The program sim doesn't catch it either. `sim_clause` only blocks on `gouge_cells` (below the model), and stock_sim's header says "Rapids touch nothing on the field ... a rapid through steel is the generation-time rapid verdict's to refuse".
- Scenario: one setup with Adaptive1 (12 mm rough) then Adaptive2 (4 mm, rest machining on), whose keep-down links rapid at low Z across the pocket Adaptive1 cleared. The user suppresses Adaptive1 and posts on a fresh blank. Adaptive2 posts G0 moves through solid stock and slots full-width with a 4 mm tool. No gate says a word.
- RECOMMENDED.md takes this as the debugging case ("part already cut that far"). The post can't know that, though, and the Prime Directive wants a visible refusal or diagnostic rather than a silent assumption.
- Minimum fix: in `verification_report`, refuse by name when a posted op's `ahead_of` set holds a suppressed op that cuts. For example, "operation Adaptive2 was generated against the cut of suppressed Adaptive1; unsuppress it or suppress Adaptive2 too". If the debugging case must stay, make it an explicit per-post opt-in that the NC header states, not the default.

### BLOCKING 2: a post that doesn't read `PARAM AfterOperation` silently drops the stop or home
- The engine passes `AfterOperation` to `onParameter` and nothing checks that the script acted on it. A user `.cps`, or any post without `afterOp()`, posts an op set to Program stop / Optional stop / Go home with no M0/M1/G28.
- The operator programmed a stop (to flip a part, clear chips or measure) and the machine runs straight into the next tool. That is wrong output with no diagnostic. It's the same class #231 closes for coolant with `coolantModes`.
- Fix: a manifest flag (for example `afterModes = true`) in the six shipped posts. Have the engine refuse any `PARAM AfterOperation` by name ("operation X: asks <stop>, but this post does not read AfterOperation") for a script without it.

### Non-blocking
- Fanuc with G43.4 (TCPM) armed: `afterOp()` runs before the `tcpmOn = false` reset. G49 only comes with the next preamble, so `G91 G28 Z0` is commanded with TCPM still on. Many controls alarm or move unexpectedly on a reference return under TCPM. Suggest `if (tcpmOn) block(["G49"])` (or G49 always) ahead of the home blocks.
- The Heidenhain home refusal doesn't name the op. #231 makes the coolant refusals start with `operation <name>:`; worth matching here.
- Go home on the last op homes twice, because onClose homes again. It's harmless.

No unwrap/expect outside tests. Commands are undoable (`with_suppressed`, `SetPostOptions`). Clean-room provenance lines are present.

Back to draft: this PR carries `needs-rework` and `conflicts` (review findings open, branch conflicts with main), so it is not ready under AGENTS.md's draft rule. It returns to ready once the findings are fixed, main is merged in, its gate is green and a fresh independent review is clean.

Answers to the review of 70f053d. Fixes are in 6a8511e, on top of the main merge 5523748.

**BLOCKING 1: suppressed op ahead of a dependent.** Fixed. `posting::verification_report` has a new suppression clause (`crates/app/src/posting_suppressed.rs`). It looks at each posted op whose verdicts read the program ahead (`operation::reads_prior`). If a suppressed op ahead of it in its setup cut something (`rest::suppressed_cuts_ahead`: a non-empty path, not a probe), the post refuses and names both ops: `operation Rest2 was generated against the cut of suppressed Rough1; unsuppress Rough1 or suppress Rest2 too`. The per-op post goes through the same gate. The debugging case is dropped, not kept as an opt-in; the reasons are in docs/decisions/110-pause-home.md. Pinned by `suppressed_rest::suppressing_a_cut_a_later_op_was_generated_against_refuses_by_name` (rough, then a rest pass; suppress the rough; the combined post and the per-op post both refuse and write nothing) and `suppressing_an_op_nothing_depends_on_still_posts`.

**BLOCKING 2: a post that doesn't read AfterOperation.** Fixed. There is now an `afterModes = true` manifest flag, following the `coolantModes` pattern. The six shipped posts that write `afterOp()` declare it. For a script without it, the engine refuses any `PARAM AfterOperation` and names the op: `operation X: asks a program stop after it, but this post script does not declare afterModes ...`. That warning is counted and holds the post. Heidenhain still refuses Go home. Tormach is new on main and has no `afterOp()`, so it refuses the ask. Pinned by `post_engine::a_stop_asked_of_a_script_without_after_modes_is_refused_by_name`, which posts the same script once without the flag (refused) and once with it (M0 is written).

**Non-blocking**
- TCPM before Go home on Fanuc: done. `if (tcpmOn) { block(["G49"]); tcpmOn = false; }` now runs ahead of the reference-return blocks.
- The Heidenhain home refusal now names the op, and so does every post's "unknown after-operation ask" refusal.
- The double home on a last-op Go home is left as it is, since it's harmless.
- Also fixed: the coolantModes refusal text from main had a run of stray spaces inside the message.

Main is merged in (17 conflicts). The PostOptions twin is unified as `{ threading, skip_stops, per_op }`. The full gate readings are in the PR body. The PR stays a draft until a fresh independent review.

**Estimated agent cost:** ~$3.62 (rough estimate from size: 2102 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
